newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian share market cap hits record A$440 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australian share market cap hits record A$440 bln.

text.p: The market capitalisation of domestic companies listed on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) reached a record A$440 billion at the close of trade on Monday, the last day of fiscal 1996/97, the ASX said.
This represented a 27 percent increase on the year earlier level, the ASX said.
It said equities trading also reached record breaking levels in 1996/97, surpassing any previous financial or calendar year.
Turnover for the year ended Monday reached a record A$212 billion, topping the 1995/96 turnover of A$159 billion by 33 percent and the calendar year record of A$185.8 billion in 1996.
The key All Ordinaries share price index reached a new record closing high of 2725.9 on Monday, up 21.6 percent on the 1995/96 close, the ASX said.
The All Ordinaries Accumulation index also hit a high of 1154.1 on Monday, up 26.5 percent on the year-earlier level.
June trading was also a record at more than A$22 billion, which topped the previous monthly record of A$20.5 billion reached in May, the ASX said.
June's average daily trade of A$1.14 billion was also a record.
The year's turnover included about A$1.3 billion in warrants trading, up from A$527 million in 1995/96, the ASX said.
The volume of warrants traded rose 400 percent in the past year, it said.
Market liquidity for the financial year reached 55 percent, an increase on 48 percent in 1995/96, the ASX added.
